findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced this morning." followed by a `<ul>` containing only 3 `<li>` items (Beta Launch Plan, Holiday Campaign Assets, Partner Integration Pilot)
findings.fix: Either add the missing 4th project to the list, correct the count in the paragraph to "3 projects", or add explicit text such as "showing 3 most recent" to clarify the list is not exhaustive.
findings.violation: The stated project count (4) does not match the number of projects actually listed (3), and there is no indication that the list is a partial/"recent" subset.

findings.violation: The listed project names are plain text, not links, so there is no way to navigate into any specific project from the overview.

findings.evidence: `<button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` with no subsequent confirmation section or link
findings.fix: Add a "settings saved" confirmation section/state (or toast equivalent) reachable after Save, matching the pattern used for invite-member.
findings.violation: Saving project settings has no resulting confirmation state, unlike the analogous invite flow which leads to a dedicated "Invite sent" section - an inconsistent and dead-end interaction.

findings.fix: Add visible text (e.g., "Duplicate") or an icon with accompanying visible label to the button.
findings.violation: The button has no visible text content or icon, only an `aria-label`, so sighted users see an empty, unlabeled clickable element.

findings.evidence: The duplicate button exists with no corresponding confirmation step or resulting "project duplicated" section, whereas `archive-confirm`/`project-archived` provide both for the comparably consequential Archive action
findings.fix: Add a confirmation step and/or a result state (e.g., a "Project duplicated" section or redirect to the new project's settings) for the Duplicate action.
findings.violation: Duplicating a project (an action that creates new data) has no confirmation and no visible outcome anywhere in the document, making the flow incomplete relative to the similarly weighted Archive flow.

findings.fix: Consolidate into a single "Send invite" action, or clearly differentiate the two (e.g., label the submit button "Send invite" and remove the separate "Continue" link, or explain what Save persists before sending).
findings.violation: It's unclear what "Save" does versus "Continue," since the invite is apparently sent only after clicking "Continue" (per the "Invite sent" copy), making "Save" a redundant or confusing control with no defined effect.

findings.evidence: `<button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` with no confirmation section or link afterward
findings.fix: Add a confirmation state/section after saving notification settings, consistent with how other completed actions (invite, archive) confirm success.
findings.violation: As with project-settings, saving notification preferences has no resulting confirmation state, leaving the action a dead end.
